question: medium-tier full-population points on both domains (union-store protocol)
design: official medium tier gives each question a distinct 500-trajectory subset; official harness builds fresh per-question memory. This run seeds each domain's union once (enterprise 874 trajectories / 33,212 docs, web union similar) and answers every question against it - a superset haystack, so retrieval faces more distractors than the official per-question setting and accuracy is a LOWER BOUND for the protocol. Same text-projection pipeline, orchestrated top-12, glm-5.3 answerer, deterministic evaluator specs + glm-5.3 llm judges; CPU embedding device
findings: 5x deeper haystack barely moves accuracy on the same protocol: enterprise medium 0.1943 vs small 0.1896 (+0.5pp). The misses were never about haystack depth - the structural strata (dynamic-environment, cross-state answers) dominate, so adding distractors is nearly free for what the stack already could not do.

Web-medium 0.1958 exceeds the archived web-small text arm 0.158, but the protocols differ (this run: glm-5.3 answerer via run_lme_v2.py; the archived arm: glm-5.3-flash via the mm runner) - not a comparable pair; the same-protocol enterprise pair above is the controlled comparison.
Latency splits by corpus shape: web union docs are short (p50 2.3s), enterprise a11y states are long (p50 35.0s over 33k docs) - both inside the official [1s, 200s] band.
web procedure 0.381 is the best stratum anywhere in V2 for this stack; web dynamic-environment-abs 0.048 the worst.
honest_reading: union-store superset setting (lower bound); 12/211 enterprise and 33/240 web answers are empty generation degradations scored wrong (web 13.8% - worth a degradation-path look); glm-5.3 same-family answerer+judge; CPU device. LAFS (official formula): medium reference 51.0741, both points gain exactly 0.0 - dominated by the RAG 45.9@0.3s floor at every budget; the frontier gap remains accuracy, not latency.
